answer: Identity here is capital at risk, not a name. Before an agent votes or earns, it must post a bond a challenger can seize, locked long enough that exit is slow. Running many fake agents is no longer cheap: each sybil identity needs its own full bond, and one proven fraud case burns all of it, so the attacker pays a whole clone fleet to gain one voice. Weighting influence by locked stake makes the attack a mesa of burned capital, while honest agents keep their deposit, like a crystal surviving review, and real participation flows like a steady tide that grows the pool instead of draining it.
